claim_text: The safety and wellbeing of our employees, contractors and communities is core to our values, and to what we stand for as a company. Nothing matters more.
metric_name: Fatalities at managed operations; All-injury frequency rate; Potential fatal incidents
context_text: The safety and wellbeing of our employees, contractors and communities is core to our values, and to what we stand for as a company. Nothing matters more.；Tragically, in August 2025, our colleague Mohamed Camara was fatally injured while changing a heavy mobile equipment tyre at the SimFer mine site in Guinea.；We recorded 87 potential fatal incidents (PFIs) during the year.；Fatalities at managed operations 1 (2024: 5 fatalities).；All-injury frequency rate (AIFR) at 0.37 (target: 0.38). (2024: 0.37).
label: Suspected Greenwash
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that employee/contractor/community safety and wellbeing is the company’s top priority (“core to our values… Nothing matters more”). The evidence provides some substantive safety performance context—1 fatality at managed operations (down from 5 in 2024), 87 potential fatal incidents, and an all-injury frequency rate of 0.37 per 200,000 hours worked versus a target of 0.38 (and equal to 2024’s 0.37). However, these metrics do not substantively verify the value-based superlative that “nothing matters more,” nor do they demonstrate how safety is prioritized over other values or outcomes across employees, contractors, and communities. The evidence supports that safety is tracked and reported with specific results, but it does not fully substantiate the claim’s absolute prioritization language.
